edges.description: Loss of cochlear hair cell transduction causes sensorineural hearing loss.
When the Usher protein is required for hair-bundle development, transduction failure is present from birth, producing congenital sensorineural hearing loss (USH1/USH2).
Loss of vestibular hair cell transduction causes vestibular areflexia, most pronounced in USH1.
Vestibular areflexia delays motor development and independent walking in USH1.
intermediate_mechanisms: impaired postural and balance control in infancy

edges.description: Impaired ciliary transport and outer-segment maintenance cause progressive photoreceptor loss.
Progressive photoreceptor loss manifests clinically as retinitis pigmentosa.
Progressive peripheral photoreceptor loss constricts the visual field.

nodes.description: Disruption of the tip-link and hair-bundle architecture prevents deflection-gated opening of the mechanotransduction channel, so hair cells cannot convert sound-evoked or head-movement-evoked bundle deflection into a receptor potential. The result is sensorineural hearing loss and, in USH1, vestibular areflexia.

evidence.reference_title: Usher Syndrome: Genetics and Molecular Links of Hearing Loss and Directions for Therapy.
evidence.snippet: Disease-causing mutations in USH genes can destabilize the tip links that bind the stereocilia to each other, and cause defects in protein trafficking and stereocilia bundle morphology, thereby inhibiting mechanosensory transduction.

nodes.description: Pdzd7 knockdown produces an Usher-like phenotype and worsens retinal-cell death when combined with ush2a or gpr98 perturbation. It supports genetic interaction and retinal-modifier biology but does not reproduce the full human auditory-retinal disease or distinguish all classical subtypes.

evidence.reference_title: PDZD7 is a modifier of retinal disease and a contributor to digenic Usher syndrome.
evidence.snippet: We validated the human genotypes using zebrafish, and our findings were consistent with digenic inheritance of PDZD7 and GPR98, and with PDZD7 as a retinal disease modifier in patients with USH2A.

nodes.description: Usher proteins are also expressed at the photoreceptor periciliary and connecting-cilium region, where they participate in protein trafficking between the inner and outer segments. Model evidence suggests that disruption can impair light-dependent protein translocation and intersegmental trafficking; the precise contribution and strength of this mechanism vary by Usher protein.

nodes.description: Progressive rod-then-cone photoreceptor degeneration produces the clinical picture of retinitis pigmentosa: nyctalopia and peripheral visual field constriction first, followed by central acuity loss.

evidence.snippet: RP, a progressive bilateral symmetric degeneration of photoreceptors in the retina, develops in early adolescence, resulting in progressively constricted visual fields first, due to rod photoreceptor cell loss, followed by impaired visual acuity due to cone photoreceptor cell loss.

nodes.description: Progressive retinitis pigmentosa is a defining retinal feature across the three classical Usher subtypes, with variable onset and course.

nodes.description: Counsel against tobacco smoking and recommend sunglasses and a cap to limit bright-light exposure as modifiable precautions for retinitis pigmentosa.

evidence.reference_title: Usher Syndrome Type I.
evidence.snippet: Exposure to bright sunlight and smoking tobacco can accelerate progression of RP. Refrain from smoking and avoid exposing eyes to sunlight by wearing sunglasses and a cap.

nodes.description: Investigational antisense oligonucleotide (AON) that induces skipping of USH2A exon 13, which contains the recurrent c.2299delG and c.2276G>T pathogenic variants. Exon skipping is intended to produce a shortened usherin protein. Preclinical zebrafish and patient-derived photoreceptor-precursor studies support the splice-modulation concept; ultevursen is being evaluated by intravitreal injection in the Phase 2b LUNA trial.

evidence.reference_title: Antisense oligonucleotide-based treatment of retinitis pigmentosa caused by USH2A exon 13 mutations.
evidence.snippet: Mutations in USH2A are among the most common causes of syndromic and non-syndromic retinitis pigmentosa (RP). The two most recurrent mutations in USH2A, c.2299delG and c.2276G > T, both reside in exon 13.

evidence.reference_title: Antisense oligonucleotide-based treatment of retinitis pigmentosa caused by USH2A exon 13 mutations.
evidence.snippet: Lead candidate QR-421a induced a concentration-dependent exon 13 skipping in induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived photoreceptor precursors from an Usher syndrome patient homozygous for the c.2299delG mutation.

evidence.reference_title: A Two-Year Double-masked, Randomized, Sham-Controlled Study to Evaluate the Efficacy, Safety and Tolerability of Ultevursen in Subjects With Retinitis Pigmentosa (RP) Due to Mutations in Exon 13 of the USH2A Gene
evidence.snippet: The purpose of this Phase 2b study is to evaluate the safety and tolerability of ultevursen administered via intravitreal injection (IVT) in subjects with Retinitis Pigmentosa (RP) due to mutations in exon 13 of the USH2A gene.

nodes.description: The Usher proteins (myosin VIIa, harmonin, cadherin-23, protocadherin-15, sans, usherin, ADGRV1/VLGR1, whirlin, clarin-1) form an interconnected network that builds and maintains the cohesion of the stereocilia hair bundle in cochlear and vestibular hair cells. Cadherin-23 and protocadherin-15 constitute the tip-link that gates the mechanotransduction channel, while harmonin, sans, and myosin VIIa anchor the link complex and stabilize bundle architecture during development. Loss of Usher-complex function can disrupt hair-bundle morphogenesis or tip-link organization and mechanotransduction.
nodes.id: Usher Interactome Disruption in the Hair Bundle

evidence.reference_title: Usher protein functions in hair cells and photoreceptors.
evidence.snippet: In mature hair cells, homodimers of the Usher cadherins, cadherin 23 and protocadherin 15, interact to form a structural fiber, the tip link, and the linkages that anchor the taller stereocilia's actin cytoskeleton core to the shorter adjacent stereocilia and the elusive mechanotransduction channels, explaining the deafness phenotype when these molecular interactions are perturbed.

evidence.reference_title: Usher syndrome: molecular links of pathogenesis, proteins and pathways.
evidence.snippet: The localization of the Usher proteins and the phenotype in animal models indicate that the Usher protein complex is essential in the morphogenesis of the stereocilia bundle in hair cells and in the calycal processes of photoreceptor cells.

nodes.description: Biallelic pathogenic variants disrupt the relevant Usher protein and its tissue-specific protein complex. Across the classical subtypes, these complexes support structures in both sensory-hair bundles and photoreceptor calycal/periciliary regions; the two tissue effects are parallel branches, not a causal sequence from ear to retina.
